claim: `SYSTEM CAS GC RUN [ON CLUSTER cluster_name] [disk_name]` runs one synchronous, node-local garbage-collection round for content-addressed `MergeTree` disks and reclaims objects no longer referenced by any part.
In `SYSTEM CAS GC RUN`, specifying `disk_name` restricts the round to that content-addressed disk; specifying a non-content-addressed disk raises an exception.
When `disk_name` is omitted from `SYSTEM CAS GC RUN`, one round runs on every content-addressed disk configured on the node, and the command raises an exception if none are configured.
Each `SYSTEM CAS GC RUN` round is recorded in `system.cas_gc_log` as `Start` and `Finish` rows with `trigger = 'Manual'`.

`SYSTEM CAS GC RUN` returns one result row per disk with the columns `disk`, `acquired_lease`, `deferred`, `round`, `candidates_marked`, `objects_deleted`, `objects_absent`, `objects_replaced`, `objects_spared`, `manifests_deleted`, `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, `entries_redeleted`, `fence_outs`, and `anomalies`.

`SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD [FORCE] [ON CLUSTER cluster_name] disk_name` rebuilds a CAS disk's `gc/state` baseline by rediscovering the complete ref universe and refolding manifest edges into a fresh generation.
`SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` writes only the GC plane, namely `gc/state` and `gc/gen/*` artifacts, and does not touch ref shards, manifests, or blobs or delete anything during the rebuild itself.
An incorrect `SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` can cause a later GC round to delete still-referenced objects because the rebuilt baseline drives subsequent retire decisions.

`SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` requires `disk_name` and raises an exception when directed at a non-content-addressed disk; it never fans out from a bare command across all content-addressed disks on the node.

Without `FORCE`, `SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` refuses to run when the existing `gc/state` and all referenced artifacts are present and decode successfully; `FORCE` deliberately overrides that healthy-state refusal.
`SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` refuses and raises an exception, regardless of `FORCE`, when another GC leader holds the disk lease.

A successful `SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` returns `disk`, `performed`, `round`, `generation`, `namespaces`, `shards`, `committed_refs`, `live_precommits`, `unowned_alive_manifests`, `edges`, and `clamped_shards`.

`SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER 'server_root_id' FROM DISK 'disk_name' [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]` permanently decommissions a dead content-addressed pool member by claiming its mount slot as an administrative writer, fencing that `server_root_id`, dropping its table namespaces, draining eligible debris, and retiring the slot after confirmed drains.

`SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` is a writer operation that emits ordinary ref-edge deltas and does not synchronously reclaim shared blob content; removing the edges makes those blobs eligible for a later ordinary GC round.

Both `server_root_id` and `disk_name` are required string literals for `SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER`; `server_root_id` is an opaque server-root path that may contain `/` and therefore cannot be written as an unquoted identifier.
`SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` is resumable: reruns skip namespaces already marked `Removed` and report them separately from namespaces newly removed by the current invocation.

Per-object drain failures during `SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` are recorded as warnings and leave the slot in a terminated-but-not-fully-drained state that a later invocation can resume, rather than raising an exception.

`SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` returns `server_root_id`, `namespaces_removed`, `namespaces_already_removed`, `committed_refs_removed`, `precommits_removed`, `manifest_debris_removed`, `staging_objects_removed`, `mountpoint_objects_removed`, `slot_removed`, and `warnings`.
A non-empty `warnings` result from `SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` means some drain was not confirmed and the mount slot remains as a resume anchor.
The CAS metric registry contained 165 `Cas*` metric names before the naming change: 156 from `ProfileEvents.cpp` and 9 from `CurrentMetrics.cpp`.
CAS metric names were normalized from the `Cas` prefix to `CAS`, while compare-and-swap tail identifiers were renamed to use `CompareSwap`.
CAS metric filters in `dump_cas_metrics.py`, `scenarios/framework/observe.py`, and `smoke_relink_validate.sh` use `LIKE 'CAS%'` after the metric-prefix normalization.
The asynchronous CAS metric format strings are `CASGcIsLeader_{}`, `CASGcPendingReclaim_{}`, `CASGcLastSuccessAgeSeconds_{}`, and `CASGcWedgedNamespaces_{}`.
The live event is `CASRefNeedsRecovery`, emitted by `CasRefLedger::requireRecovery`; `CasRefApplyPoisoned` was never present in `src/Common/ProfileEvents.cpp` or `CurrentMetrics.cpp`.
The stale `CasRefApplyPoisoned` probe caused the S38 run `20260729T115218` to raise because the binary did not expose the probed counters.

The soak tooling's stale `CasRefApplyPoisoned` name was mapped to `CASRefNeedsRecovery`, and the stale executable needle `is POISONED at` was corrected to `NEEDS RECOVERY at` from the `CasRefLedger::requireRecovery` log text.

`CasRefRecoverySealPublished` was absent from the registry and was inferred, for collection-only tooling, to correspond to `CASRefRecoveryEpochSealed`; the mapping was not code-stated and did not affect a card verdict.

The `utils/ca-soak` text-log probe using `logger_name = 'CasStore'` is unresolved because neither the `CasStore` logger nor its `crossed soft limit` message exists in `src/`; it is documented as best-effort and fails open when unavailable.
Dated soak-history records retain stale names such as `CasRefApplyPoisoned` when they quote what an earlier run actually reported; historical evidence is not rewritten to current registry spelling.

The obscure CAS naming pass changed `CASGc` to `CASGC`, `CASRefCkpt` to `CASRefCheckpoint`, `UnappliedFoldedTxns` to `UnappliedFoldedTransactions`, `PutDedup` to `PutDeduplicated`, and `DedupCache` to `DeduplicationCache`.
The obscure naming pass leaves production classes `CasGc` and `CasRefCkpt` unchanged; the renames apply to metric and suite tokens rather than those class identifiers.
The async CAS metric format strings use `CASGCIsLeader_{}`, `CASGCPendingReclaim_{}`, `CASGCLastSuccessAgeSeconds_{}`, and `CASGCWedgedNamespaces_{}` after the `CASGc` to `CASGC` normalization.

The ten `CasRefCatalog::read` sites in `CasRefLedger.cpp` were classified as admission/identity resolution, mutation authority, current-life destructive revalidation, held-handle hot path, or duplicate read; the file had zero held-handle-hot-path and zero duplicate-read removal sites.

The warm path of `acquireReadableRefTableRuntime` returns the resident runtime before any catalog read, so a held-runtime read issues zero catalog GETs unless separate maintenance work such as a stale-precommit sweep is armed.

The cold `acquireReadableRefTableRuntime` admission performs a first catalog cut and a load-bearing confirmation read; if the token or decoded value changes, admission throws a retry-later exception instead of publishing a superseded runtime.
`resolveNamespaceLife` performs one catalog read per retry-loop attempt, re-observes the result after each catalog mutation attempt, and is bounded by `kMaxResolveAttempts = 32`.

The `commitRefChunk` `removal_append` arm rereads the catalog immediately before ID allocation and requires the exact catalog life to remain `Removing` before appending a terminal removal-class ref-log record.

The `commitRefChunk` `positive_append` arm performs a final catalog admission observation before ID allocation, requires the exact life to remain `Live`, and permanently closes the local positive lane when the row is not `Live`.
Before refusing a closed removal admission, `namespaceLife` reconciles a fresh catalog cut so an absent or replaced row can detach a dead predecessor and free the logical namespace name.

`dropNamespace(const NamespaceLifeId &)` rejects a stale held incarnation through the `expected_incarnation` guard and throws a retry-later exception instead of writing against a successor namespace life.
`dropNamespaceImpl` performs a fresh exact-row catalog read after the unbounded lane-drain wait and uses that observation to gate the `Live -> Removing` transition CAS.

When `beginRemoving` fails ambiguously, `dropNamespaceImpl` fails closed: it reopens the lane only after a fresh observation proves the identical original `Live` row and mount fence; every other state remains closed and the exception is rethrown.

The four read/list entry points `resolveRef`, `listRefs`, `hasAnyRefWithPrefix`, and `namespaceFilesLifeIfReadable` use `acquireReadableRefTableRuntime`; the warm held-runtime path reaches none of the ten catalog-read sites.
The only life-taking mutation entry point is `dropNamespace(const NamespaceLifeId &)`, and its stale-incarnation guard ensures a held life can never target a reborn successor namespace.
The `readable_catalog_after_observation_hook_for_test` hook is used by three `RefWriterRuntimeIdentity` tests to inject catalog changes between the cold arm's two observations; it is not unused.

After a same-name rebirth, a held readable runtime may return the old life's ref or no ref but must never return the successor life's ref; after the runtime is evicted and cold recovery runs, the same pool resolves the successor life.

Once a ref runtime is warm and stale-precommit maintenance is disarmed, `resolveRef`, `listRefs`, and `hasAnyRefWithPrefix` issue zero requests against the catalog and no counted backend requests at all.

A stale-life `store->dropNamespace(life1)` after life 2 is admitted throws `ErrorCodes::NETWORK_ERROR`, leaves the catalog token and bytes unchanged, and does not prevent an independent fresh store from resolving life 2.
Cold ref-table recovery reads the namespace checkpoint through `readCkpt` and `backend.get(layout.refCkptKey(life))`; it does not recover by listing the namespace stream prefix.
`CasPlainObjects::listNamespaceFiles` derives its LIST prefix from `layout.namespaceFilesPrefix(life)` and does not access `layout.refCatalogKey()`.

The `ListThroughHeldLifeIssuesZeroCatalogRequests` contract requires exactly one LIST of the namespace-files prefix and no other counted backend request, as enforced by `listCount(prefix) == 1`, `listTotal() == 1`, and `touchedKeys() == {prefix}`.
The `CasNamespaceFileDiskProfile.SteadyStateFileOperationsTouchNoCatalogRefBlobOrManifestKey` test does not exercise the `listNamespaceFiles` arm; direct list-arm coverage is provided separately.
The test-only namespace fixture seam is `DB::Cas::tests::fixture` and exposes `fixtureLife`, `admitLive`, and `writeRefLogRaw` as named entry points for fixture-only behavior.

`fixture::fixtureLife` creates a deterministic namespace-derived identity rather than a fresh random life, `fixture::admitLive` creates a bare `Live` entry without `_ckpt`, and `fixture::writeRefLogRaw` writes ref-log bytes directly at the resolved fixture identity while bypassing the writer birth/append lane.
The test migration maps `NamespaceLifeId::stageATransition(ns)` to `fixture::fixtureLife(ns)`, `casAdmitEntry` to `fixture::admitLive`, and `writeRefLogTxnRaw` to `fixture::writeRefLogRaw`.

The 14 migrated test sites that previously used `resolveLifeOrSentinel` had already admitted or created a catalog entry and therefore now use `CasRefCatalog::lifeIfCataloged(...).value()`, making a missing entry a hard failure.

The fixture identity derivation is byte-for-byte equivalent to `NamespaceLifeId::stageATransition`: it uses `sipHash128` over the namespace string bytes, maps a zero hash to `1`, and calls `NamespaceLifeId::fromCatalogEntry(ns, incarnation)`; existing fixture keys therefore remain unchanged.

Fixture helpers use `CasRefCatalog::lifeIfCataloged(backend, layout, ns).value_or(fixture::fixtureLife(ns))`, so an admitted catalog life wins and the deterministic fixture identity is used only when no catalog entry exists.
Production `CasRefCatalog::resolveLifeOrSentinel` and `NamespaceLifeId::stageATransition` were deleted, and source greps found no remaining non-documentation references to either name.

The GC implementation must use the same complete catalog cut for a decision and must not perform an independent catalog reread; the deleted `resolveLifeOrSentinel` helper was replaced in comments by this invariant.

`CasRefCatalogFormat.RemovalStartedRoundIsRequiredExactlyForRemoving` directly invokes a `LOGICAL_ERROR`-throwing site under `DEBUG_OR_SANITIZER_BUILD`, where the process aborts instead of throwing; the planned hygiene fix is to guard the throwing arm and add a `Cas*DeathTest` arm using `EXPECT_DEATH`.
The literal plan vocabulary `Poisoned` refers to `RefLaneState::NeedsRecovery`; there is no state literally named `Poisoned` in `CasRefLedger`.

When `tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce` encounters a `NeedsRecovery` lane, it recovers the durable gap before proceeding; recovery may issue its own `_ckpt` CAS, and a snapshot must never be published from the unrecovered cache.

For a `NeedsRecovery` publish attempt, recovery's checkpoint catch-up CAS must precede every snapshot-body PUT and the publisher's own checkpoint-advance CAS; the resulting published snapshot reflects the recovered frontier.
A normal snapshot publication writes the snapshot body before advancing the publisher checkpoint, and the body PUT and checkpoint CAS are each observed as one request for the publication attempt.

Snapshot adoption occurs only after both the snapshot body PUT and checkpoint advancement are durable; if checkpoint advancement conflicts, in-memory adoption does not occur during that failed retry unit.
`publishCkpt` has `MAX_CKPT_CAS_ATTEMPTS = 100` attempt-bounded retries.

The per-table snapshot-publish dispatch backoff starts at 1000 ms, doubles to 2000 ms, doubles again to a 4000 ms cap, and `resetPublishBackoff` clears the cooldown so a same-time over-threshold trigger dispatches immediately.
The snapshot-publish dispatch count is observable through `ProfileEvents::CasRefSnapshotPublishDispatched`.

The per-table snapshot-publish backoff driven by `RefTableRuntime::publish_backoff_ms` and `publish_backoff_until_ms` is distinct from the request controller's per-attempt retry backoff in `CasRequestControllerBackoff`.

The private methods `admitSnapshotPublishUnderStateLock`, `advancePublishBackoff`, and `resetPublishBackoff` are characterized only through the public dispatch surface `appendRefOps` or `resolveRef` leading to `maybeScheduleSnapshotPublish`; their tests assert observable dispatch behavior rather than private return values.
The real ref-lane states are `RefLaneState::Ready`, `Writing`, `Wedged`, `NeedsRecovery`, `Closed`, and `Faulted`; there are no `Clean`, `ApplyPending`, or `Poisoned` states.

The strings `CasGcIsLeader` and `CasGcPendingReclaimEntries` remain in two sites because they refer to retired process-global gauges, and changing them would invent a spelling for gauges that no longer exist.
The `CasRefGcCleanupAuthority` tests pin current-life destructive per-key `deleteExact` revalidation in the GC/cleanup layer; those class-3 catalog reads are not `CasRefLedger.cpp` sites.

`confirmExactRef` is a read-shaped API that performs zero object-store I/O and never materializes a ref-table runtime, so it reaches none of the ten `CasRefCatalog::read` sites classified in `CasRefLedger.cpp`.

After re-recovery from `NeedsRecovery`, the ref lane is `Ready`, `recoveryInstallCountForTest` has advanced, the published snapshot ID equals the durable removal transaction missing from the stale cache, and `resolveRef` for that removed ref returns absent.
